findings.title: favicon-192.png generated but never referenced in <head>
findings.evidence: SettingController resizeFavicon() writes favicon/favicon-192.png (sizes map line 269-274). The blade @php block only defines $fav16, $fav32, $fav180 and emits <link> tags for those three sizes. No $fav192/$has192 variable or <link rel="icon" sizes="192x192"> tag is present anywhere in app.blade.php.
findings.consequence: Android Chrome home-screen icons and browsers that select favicons by sizes attribute cannot find the 192×192 variant. The file is generated on disk but silently unused, directly contradicting the approved task requirement of multi-size favicon (16×16, 32×32, 180×180, 192×192).
findings.correction: In the @php block add: $fav192 = $favDir . '/favicon-192.png'; $has192 = Storage::disk('public')->exists($fav192); Then emit: @if($has192)<link rel="icon" type="image/png" sizes="192x192" href="{{ Storage::url($fav192) }}">@endif alongside the other icon link tags.

findings.title: Dead $image variable — unused assignment from $manager->read()
findings.evidence: $image = $manager->read($file->path()) is assigned at line 266 and never used. Each loop iteration independently calls $manager->read($file->path()), so the initial read is wasted and the $image variable is a latent confusion hazard: a future edit might pass $image to ->cover() (the apparent original intent), which would reuse an already-processed or encoded object rather than the fresh source.
findings.consequence: One extra GD image decode per favicon upload. Higher risk: if $image is used in a future edit, it references a potentially mutated object, producing incorrect output silently.
findings.correction: Remove the line: $image = $manager->read($file->path()); The loop already reads $file->path() fresh on every iteration.
